_source: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/about-claude/pricing fetched 2026-09-06; USD per million tokens; cache_write is the 5-minute rate. meter_weight is meter percent per list dollar relative to Sonnet 5; Fable's 1.0 is measured: the 2026-09-06 5-tick Fable probe cost $1.08 of list value per 1% against $0.98 for Sonnet on the same cache-write-heavy payload (ratio 0.91, within probe error). class_weight is meter percent per list dollar for each token class relative to cache_write, the class the Sonnet probe is made of. class_weight.output is maintained by the publisher (tracker/weight.py): the weekly Sunday Fable output run (bin/output-probe.sh, payload output) supplies a row, and the next daily publish solves the weight at which that row and the latest Fable prose row read the same meter dollars per 1%, writes it to every model here, and records the pair under _output_weight; a value more than 30% from the current one is refused, recorded with applied false, and alerts Jonathan instead. The 1.8 hand-entered on 2026-09-06 was the crude ratio of the two rows' list values; the first automatic recompute from the same pair gave 1.95 because the output row's own cache traffic (12% of its list value) sits on the unweighted side. input and cache_read are unmeasured and assumed 1.0; the same class weights are assumed for every model. Opus 5's 1.0 is measured too: a paired run on the Jono Work account on 2026-09-08, same 5-hour window, cost $0.918 of list value per 1% for Opus (ticks 7 to 10) against $0.963 for Sonnet (ticks 2 to 5), ratio 0.954, within probe error, so Opus keeps meter_weight 1.0. The first Opus row (2026-09-07 on Dave, $0.682 per 1%, early tick) is flagged outlier by hand under the rotation's own decide rule: the later same-model reading agreed with the all-model median, not with it. cache_read is 0.0 since 2026-09-16, measured on masterrig: over 111 idle-bounded windows (tools/idle_burst.py, 18 Aug to 15 Sep, $4,759 of list value against 2,214 meter points) the list value per 1% climbs with the cache_read share of the window (median $1.67 at a 25-45% share, $2.69 at 45-60%, $3.28 at 60-75%, $6.13 above 75%) while the non-cache_read value per 1% holds at $1.11, $1.15, $1.25, $1.43 across the same bins ($0.94 aggregate), and a non-negative least squares fit gives cache_read a weight of 0.000 in every configuration tried. The probe never saw this because its payload is 98% cache_write by list value. output 1.8 still rests on the single 2026-09-06 output run; the same windows read $1.94 per 1% for Fable with it and $1.38 with output at 1.0, against the probe's $1.00, so the output weight is the remaining open question and the Sunday output probe is the measurement that settles it.
